title: The Fast, Luminous Ultraviolet Transient AT2018cow: Extreme Supernova, or Disruption of a Star by an Intermediate-Mass Black Hole? (Perley et al. 2019)

episodes.description: Observe AT2018cow across UV/optical/NIR photometry and spectroscopy and weigh physical origins (SN variants vs IMBH TDE)

chain.op: discovery and pre-explosion limits from ATLAS/ZTF/ASAS-SN
ground-based imaging with host-galaxy image subtraction and calibration
Swift UVOT/XRT photometry with host subtraction in flux space
add public/literature photometry (GROND, ATLAS, ZTF, ASAS-SN)
high-cadence spectroscopic monitoring and flux/colour calibration of spectra
describe spectral evolution and line identifications
fit blackbody plus power-law SEDs per epoch
host galaxy SED fit with LePhare
compare light curve and spectra to other transient classes
evaluate IMBH TDE model with scaling relation and MOSFiT MCMC

notes: Single-object explain seed. Rich per_object explain branches with named rejected causes (Ic-BL, IIn, 56Ni, shock cooling, NS merger, WD, afterglow wash-out, dust, beaming). Final cause not adjudicated. Two intervene branches (campaign, spectroscopic cadence). The one quantitative forward-model fit (MOSFiT) was applied to only one hypothesis after relaxing model constraints. X-ray/radio channels in companion papers.
